question: Which is the jet stream that brings Western disturbances in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Westerly jet stream.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Western Disturbances are brought to India by the subtropical Westerly jet stream. These are extratropical storms originating in the Mediterranean/Caspian Sea region and carried eastward by the westerlies. (पश्चिमी विक्षोभ — पछुआ जेट धारा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Western Disturbances bring winter rainfall to the north-western plains (Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, western UP) and snowfall to the Himalayas.

• This winter rain (mahawat) is very beneficial for rabi crops, especially wheat.

NOTE

• A jet stream is a narrow band of very fast winds high in the atmosphere. The subtropical westerly jet stream also influences the onset/withdrawal of the Indian monsoon.

question: Aparna Satheesan, a recipient of 2021 Abhinandan Saroja National award by National Institute of Classical Dance, is an exponent of ________ and Kuchipudi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Aparna Satheesan, a recipient of the 2021 Abhinandan Saroja National Award, is an exponent of Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi. (भरतनाट्यम और कुचिपुड़ी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni.

• Kuchipudi is the classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India/UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: According to Census of India 2011, which pair of states recorded the highest population density (persons/km2) in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar and West Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, among the states, Bihar (1,106 persons/km²) had the highest population density, followed by West Bengal (1,028 persons/km²). (बिहार और पश्चिम बंगाल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Among Union Territories, Delhi had the highest density (about 11,320 persons/km²).

• Arunachal Pradesh had the lowest population density (17 persons/km²) among the states.

NOTE

• Population density = total population / total area (persons per km²). India's overall density as per Census 2011 was 382 persons/km².

question: Identify the place where the West Central Railway Zone headquarters is located.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jabalpur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The headquarters of the West Central Railway (WCR) zone is located at Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh). (पश्चिम मध्य रेलवे — जबलपुर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The West Central Railway was formed in 2003 and has divisions at Jabalpur, Bhopal and Kota.

• Indian Railways is divided into zones, each headed by a General Manager.

NOTE

• Some zonal HQs: Central Railway – Mumbai; Northern – New Delhi; Western – Mumbai; Southern – Chennai; Eastern – Kolkata; North Central – Prayagraj.

question: Which of the following Rashtrakuta rulers performed the ceremony called ‘Hiranya Garbha’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dantidurga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rashtrakuta ruler Dantidurga (the founder of the dynasty) performed the ritual known as "Hiranya-garbha" (the golden-womb ceremony), a symbolic rite of rebirth to elevate one's status. (दंतिदुर्ग — हिरण्यगर्भ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dantidurga founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty in the 8th century CE, with its capital at Manyakheta (Malkhed).

• The famous Kailasa temple at Ellora was built by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.

NOTE

• The Hiranyagarbha ceremony was performed by the priests to grant kshatriya (royal) status. It is mentioned in relation to legitimising kingship.

question: Who can exercise a casting vote in the case of an equality of votes in Lok Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Speaker of Lok Sabha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha can exercise a casting vote in the case of a tie (equality of votes). Normally the Speaker does not vote, but in a tie he/she casts the deciding vote. (लोकसभा अध्यक्ष — निर्णायक मत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• This power is provided under Article 100 of the Constitution.

• In the Rajya Sabha, the Vice President (ex-officio Chairman) exercises the casting vote in a tie.

NOTE

• The Speaker is elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members; the first Speaker of independent India was G. V. Mavalankar. The Speaker decides whether a bill is a Money Bill.

question: The autobiography of Sam Pitroda is called:
option_2: Dreaming Big: My Journey to Connect India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dreaming Big: My Journey to Connect India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dreaming Big: My Journey to Connect India" is the autobiography of Sam Pitroda (Satyanarayan Gangaram Pitroda), the telecom pioneer often called the "Father of India's telecom/IT revolution". (सैम पित्रोदा की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Sam Pitroda played a key role in the C-DOT (Centre for Development of Telematics) and the spread of PCOs/STD booths in India in the 1980s.

• He headed the National Knowledge Commission.

NOTE

• "In the Afternoon of Time" is by Harivansh Rai Bachchan; "The Substance and the Shadow" is Dilip Kumar's autobiography; "Beyond the Lines" is Kuldip Nayar's autobiography.

question: On which of the following dates did the British Empire transfer its powers to the Constituent Assembly in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15th August.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On 15th August 1947, the British Empire transferred its powers to the Constituent Assembly of India, and India became independent. (15 अगस्त 1947)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Indian Independence Act 1947 provided for the partition of British India into the two dominions of India and Pakistan and the transfer of power.

• The Constituent Assembly (formed in 1946) became the sovereign law-making body; Jawaharlal Nehru became the first Prime Minister.

NOTE

• Key dates: 26 January 1950 – Constitution came into force (Republic Day); 26 November 1949 – Constitution adopted; 15 August 1947 – Independence Day.

question: The Right to Freedom of Religion is covered under which Articles of the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Articles 25-28.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Right to Freedom of Religion is guaranteed under Articles 25 to 28 of the Constitution of India. (धर्म की स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 25-28)

◦ Article 25 – Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion.

◦ Article 26 – Freedom to manage religious affairs.

◦ Article 27 – Freedom from taxes for promotion of a particular religion.

◦ Article 28 – Freedom from religious instruction in State-funded institutions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• These form one of the six Fundamental Rights guaranteed by the Constitution (Part III).

NOTE

• The six Fundamental Rights: Right to Equality (14–18), Right to Freedom (19–22), Right against Exploitation (23–24), Right to Freedom of Religion (25–28), Cultural & Educational Rights (29–30), Right to Constitutional Remedies (32).

question: A little child is a very picky eater and hates drinking milk and milk products. When he lost his baby tooth, permanent teeth took a very long time to come up in its place. What could be the probable reason behind this?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcium Deficiency.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As the child avoids milk and milk products (the richest sources of calcium), the delayed growth of teeth is most likely due to calcium deficiency. Calcium is essential for the formation of strong teeth and bones. (कैल्शियम की कमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Calcium deficiency can cause weak bones, delayed tooth development, and osteoporosis.

• Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium; milk is often fortified with Vitamin D.

NOTE

• Rich sources of calcium: milk, cheese, curd, green leafy vegetables, and ragi. Calcium also helps in blood clotting and muscle contraction.

question: The 'Quit India Movement' was launched under the leadership of __________________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Quit India Movement" was launched on 8 August 1942 in Bombay under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi, who gave the famous slogan "Do or Die". (भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन — महात्मा गांधी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The movement was launched after the failure of the Cripps Mission (1942).

• The All India Congress Committee passed the Quit India Resolution at its Bombay session; most top leaders were arrested immediately.

NOTE

• It is also called the August Kranti (August Revolution). Leaders like Aruna Asaf Ali, Ram Manohar Lohia and Jayaprakash Narayan kept the movement alive underground.

question: On May 23, 2023, who assumed the position of Chairperson at the Competition Commission of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ravneet Kaur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On 23 May 2023, Ravneet Kaur assumed office as the Chairperson of the Competition Commission of India (CCI). (रवनीत कौर — भारतीय प्रतिस्पर्धा आयोग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Competition Commission of India (CCI) was established under the Competition Act, 2002, and became fully functional in 2009.

• Its headquarters is in New Delhi. It works to promote fair competition and prevent monopolistic/anti-competitive practices.

NOTE

• The CCI protects consumer interests and ensures freedom of trade. It regulates mergers and acquisitions that may harm competition.

question: Which of the following Indian philosophical systems and its widely acknowledged proponents is INCORRECTLY paired?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vaisheshika - Vyasa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The pair "Vaisheshika - Vyasa" is incorrect. The Vaisheshika school was founded by Kanada (Rishi Kanada), not Vyasa. (वैशेषिक — कणाद द्वारा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The six orthodox (āstika) schools of Indian philosophy and their founders:

◦ Samkhya – Kapila; Yoga – Patanjali; Nyaya – Gautama (Gotama); Vaisheshika – Kanada; Purva Mimamsa – Jaimini; Uttara Mimamsa (Vedanta) – Vyasa (Badarayana).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

NOTE

• The Vaisheshika school is known for its atomic theory (Paramanu) — that all matter is made of tiny, indivisible atoms.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are true about public goods?

I. Rivalrous in consumption
II. Non-excludability
III. Positive marginal cost
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A public good has two defining features: it is non-rivalrous (one person's use does not reduce availability to others) and non-excludable (no one can be prevented from using it). So only statement II (Non-excludability) is true. (सार्वजनिक वस्तुएँ — गैर-अपवर्जनीय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Statement I is wrong — public goods are non-rivalrous, not rivalrous.

• Statement III is wrong — public goods generally have a zero marginal cost of providing to an additional user.

• Examples of public goods: national defence, street lighting, public parks, lighthouses.

NOTE

• Because of non-excludability, public goods suffer from the "free-rider problem", which is why they are usually provided by the government.

question: Which of the following folk dances of Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal region is on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhau.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chhau" — a semi-classical martial dance of the Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal region — was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010. (छऊ नृत्य — यूनेस्को)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Chhau has three styles: Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand), Purulia Chhau (West Bengal) and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha).

• It often depicts themes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and local folklore, and uses masks (except Mayurbhanj).

NOTE

• Other Indian entries on UNESCO's Intangible Heritage list include Kutiyattam, Ramlila, Vedic chanting, Yoga, Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja in Kolkata, and Garba of Gujarat.

question: Where did the IBA Women's World Boxing Championships 2023 take place in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The IBA Women's World Boxing Championships 2023 were held in New Delhi, India (in March 2023). (आईबीए महिला विश्व मुक्केबाज़ी चैंपियनशिप 2023 — नई दिल्ली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India won 4 gold medals at the event — through Nikhat Zareen, Lovlina Borgohain, Saweety Boora and Nitu Ghanghas.

• The championship is organised by the International Boxing Association (IBA).

NOTE

• Nikhat Zareen (born in Nizamabad, Telangana) is a two-time World Champion. Lovlina Borgohain won a bronze medal at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.

question: The rifle (in the shooting sport) is single-loaded in _________-millimetre calibre (the inner diameter of a gun barrel), which is used across all events.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.6.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the shooting sport, the rifle is single-loaded in 5.6-millimetre calibre (equivalent to .22 inch), which is used across all rifle events. (5.6 मिमी कैलिबर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Calibre" refers to the internal diameter of the gun barrel (or the diameter of the bullet).

• Olympic rifle and pistol shooting events use .22 calibre (5.6 mm) ammunition for events like the 10m air rifle, 50m rifle 3 positions, etc.

NOTE

• India's notable shooters include Abhinav Bindra (2008 Olympic gold, 10m air rifle), Gagan Narang, Manu Bhaker and Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore.

question: In Harappan civilisation, which material was NOT used in the construction of buildings?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iron.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Harappan (Indus Valley) Civilisation did NOT use iron — iron was still unknown to them. They built with burnt/baked bricks, mud bricks, wood and gypsum mortar. (हड़प्पा सभ्यता — लोहे का प्रयोग नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Harappans were a Bronze Age civilisation; they used copper and bronze but not iron.

• They were famous for standardised burnt bricks in the ratio 4:2:1 and advanced town planning.

NOTE

• Iron technology came later, in the Vedic/Later Vedic period (around 1000 BCE), marking the start of the Iron Age in India.

question: The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was enacted in which year by the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2013.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was enacted by the Government of India in 2013. It provides subsidised food grains to about two-thirds of India's population. (राष्ट्रीय खाद्य सुरक्षा अधिनियम — 2013)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Under the NFSA, eligible households get 5 kg of food grain per person per month at subsidised prices (rice ₹3, wheat ₹2, coarse grains ₹1 per kg) through the Public Distribution System (PDS).

• It covers 75% of the rural and 50% of the urban population.

NOTE

• The Act also provides maternity benefits and meals for pregnant/lactating women and children (through the ICDS and Mid-Day Meal schemes). It is also called the "Right to Food Act".

question: As of July 2023, how many products were notified under the 'One District, One Product' scheme as per the information provided by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries, Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 137.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of July 2023, 137 products were notified under the "One District, One Product (ODOP)" scheme, as per the Ministry of Food Processing Industries. (एक ज़िला एक उत्पाद — 137 उत्पाद)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The ODOP initiative promotes a specific product/craft from each district to boost local economy, exports and employment.

• It is linked with the PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme.

NOTE

• ODOP encourages "Vocal for Local" and helps in branding and value addition of traditional district-specific products (like Nagpur oranges, Bhagalpur silk, etc.).

question: Vibration or wave caused by the sudden movement of tectonic plates within the earth that can travel through and around the earth is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seismic Wave.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Seismic wave" is the vibration/energy wave produced by the sudden movement of tectonic plates (as during an earthquake) that travels through and around the Earth. (भूकंपीय तरंग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Seismic waves are of two main types: Body waves (P-waves and S-waves that travel through the Earth's interior) and Surface waves (that travel along the surface and cause most damage).

• P-waves (Primary) are the fastest; S-waves (Secondary) cannot pass through liquids.

NOTE

• Seismic waves are recorded by a seismograph; their magnitude is measured on the Richter scale and intensity on the Mercalli scale. The point of origin inside the Earth is the focus/hypocentre; the point directly above on the surface is the epicentre.

question: Which of the following agreements led Mahatma Gandhi to attend the Second Round Table Conference?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gandhi Irwin Pact.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Gandhi-Irwin Pact" (signed on 5 March 1931) led Mahatma Gandhi to attend the Second Round Table Conference (1931) in London, as a representative of the Congress. (गांधी-इरविन समझौता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Under the pact, the government agreed to release political prisoners and Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement.

• The Round Table Conferences (1930, 1931, 1932) were held to discuss constitutional reforms for India.

NOTE

• The Poona Pact (1932) was between Gandhi and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar over separate electorates for the depressed classes. The Lucknow Pact (1916) was between the Congress and the Muslim League.

question: What is the primary source of energy for most ecosystems on Earth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sunlight.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sunlight (solar energy)" is the primary source of energy for most ecosystems on Earth. Green plants use sunlight in photosynthesis to produce food, forming the base of the food chain. (सूर्य का प्रकाश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• In photosynthesis, plants convert carbon dioxide + water into glucose + oxygen using sunlight and chlorophyll.

• Plants are producers (autotrophs); the energy then flows to herbivores (primary consumers) and further along the food chain.

NOTE

• Energy flow in an ecosystem is unidirectional (Sun → producers → consumers → decomposers). Only about 10% of energy is transferred to the next trophic level (the 10% law).

question: Who was the progenitor of the prolific Jaipur-Atrauli gharana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ustad Alladiya Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Alladiya Khan was the founder (progenitor) of the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana of Hindustani classical (vocal) music. (जयपुर-अतरौली घराना — उस्ताद अल्लादिया खान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A gharana is a school/lineage of music with a distinctive style, passed down through the guru-shishya parampara.

• Famous singers of the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana include Kesarbai Kerkar and Mogubai Kurdikar.

NOTE

• Other well-known gharanas of Hindustani vocal music: Gwalior, Agra, Kirana, Patiala and Rampur-Sahaswan. Ustad Vilayat Khan and Ustad Ali Akbar Khan were instrumentalists (sitar and sarod respectively).

question: 0.25 g of an organic compound gave 0.20 g of CO2 after complete combustion. The percentage composition of carbon is _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 21.82%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the combustion method for estimating carbon, the percentage of carbon is found using the formula:

◦ % of Carbon = (12 / 44) × (mass of CO₂ / mass of compound) × 100

• Here, mass of compound = 0.25 g and mass of CO₂ = 0.20 g.

◦ % C = (12 / 44) × (0.20 / 0.25) × 100

◦ % C = 0.2727 × 0.80 × 100 = 21.82%. (कार्बन का प्रतिशत — 21.82%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The factor 12/44 is used because in one molecule of CO₂ (molar mass 44), the mass of carbon is 12.

• Every 44 g of CO₂ produced corresponds to 12 g of carbon in the original compound.

NOTE

• This is based on Liebig's combustion method for the quantitative estimation of carbon and hydrogen in an organic compound. Similarly, % of Hydrogen = (2/18) × (mass of H₂O / mass of compound) × 100.
